passages.section_heading: Business travel vs temporary remote work
passages.text:
Travel to do Ridgeline work at a client, a project site or a Ridgeline office is business travel, not temporary remote work. passages.text:

passages.title: Information Security & Acceptable Use
passages.text:
Notify IT Security at least 5 working days before you start working from another country. IT Security will check that your device and access are set up for the destination, and may issue a travel laptop for the trip. This applies in addition to the HR review in RSE-LOC-01 §3.
Some destinations have rules on encryption or on carrying certain data, and some client agreements forbid access from particular countries. IT Security checks these before you go. Don't take Client Restricted paper documents abroad, and keep your devices with you while travelling. Business trips abroad follow the same notification rule when you will work on Ridgeline systems while away.

passages.title: Remote & Hybrid Work Policy
passages.text:
Temporary remote work from another US state, or another province, needs your manager's approval for up to 30 calendar days per calendar year in total. Anything over 30 calendar days in a year needs HR review: your manager can't approve it alone, and HR decides.
The 30 calendar days count every day you are away, including weekends, and they add up across all trips in the calendar year. For example, a stay from the first of one month to the tenth of the following month is well over 30 calendar days, so it needs HR review even if your manager supports it. Submit the request in the HR Portal with your dates and location; HR reviews longer stays because working in another state or province can affect payroll and tax registration.
